items.q: Visible haematuria one day into a sore throat in a young adult most suggests what?
items.exp: IgA nephropathy bleeds synpharyngitically within one to three days of mucosal infection, while post streptococcal disease waits one to three weeks. Mesangial IgA with normal complement confirms it.
r: Incorrect. Post streptococcal disease lags infection by weeks with low C3.
Correct. Same week bleeding means IgA nephropathy.
Incorrect. Minimal change causes nephrotic proteinuria without this bleeding.
Incorrect. Membranous causes adult nephrotic syndrome.
items.kp: Bleeds with the sore throat: IgA. Weeks later: post streptococcal.

items.q: Subepithelial hump deposits with low C3 normalising by eight weeks indicate which disease?
items.exp: Post streptococcal glomerulonephritis shows large subepithelial humps, neutrophil rich hypercellularity and transient C3 consumption recovering in six to eight weeks. Persistent low C3 needs another diagnosis.
r: Incorrect. IgA deposits sit in mesangium with normal C3.
Correct. Humps plus transient low C3 mean post infective disease.
Incorrect. Anti GBM stains linearly without humps.
Incorrect. Pauci immune disease deposits almost nothing.
items.kp: Humps plus recovering C3 equals post streptococcal disease.

items.q: A child with abrupt periorbital oedema, heavy proteinuria and normal biopsy light microscopy likely has what?
items.exp: Minimal change disease causes most abrupt childhood nephrotic syndrome with only podocyte foot effacement on electron microscopy and excellent steroid response. Biopsy is often deferred after steroid trial in typical children.
r: Incorrect. Membranous is an adult spike disease.
Correct. Minimal change dominates childhood nephrotic syndrome.
Incorrect. Segmental sclerosis is steroid resistant and less abrupt typically.
Incorrect. IgA causes haematuria, not pure nephrotic syndrome.
items.kp: Child plus abrupt nephrotic plus steroid response: minimal change.

items.q: PLA2R antibodies and subepithelial spikes in an adult nephrotic patient indicate which disease?
items.exp: Primary membranous nephropathy associates with anti PLA2R antibodies and granular subepithelial deposits with basement membrane spikes. Secondary causes include malignancy, hepatitis B and lupus needing screening.
r: Incorrect. Minimal change lacks deposits and spikes.
Correct. PLA2R plus spikes means membranous nephropathy.
Incorrect. Post streptococcal humps sit in nephritic children mainly.
Incorrect. Thin membranes cause benign familial haematuria.
items.kp: PLA2R positive adult nephrotic: membranous. Screen for cancer.

items.q: Pulmonary haemorrhage plus crescentic nephritis with linear IgG staining indicates what?
items.exp: Anti glomerular basement membrane antibodies stain linearly and attack lung alveolar membranes too, causing Goodpasture syndrome. Plasmapheresis plus immunosuppression is urgent.
r: Incorrect. ANCA disease is pauci immune without linear staining.
Correct. Linear staining plus lung bleed means anti GBM disease.
Incorrect. Lupus gives full house granular deposits.
Incorrect. IgA vasculitis deposits IgA with palpable purpura.
items.kp: Linear staining plus bleeding lungs: remove the antibody fast.

items.q: Pauci immune crescentic nephritis with PR3 ANCA most suggests which vasculitis?
items.exp: PR3 ANCA pauci immune crescentic disease with upper airway and lung granulomatous features is granulomatosis with polyangiitis. MPO ANCA favours microscopic polyangiitis and renal limited disease.
r: Correct. PR3 plus granulomatous airways means GPA.
Incorrect. Microscopic disease favours MPO antibodies.
Incorrect. Polyarteritis spares glomeruli and is ANCA negative.
Incorrect. Takayasu affects large aorta branches in young women.
items.kp: PR3 thinks upper airways; MPO thinks kidney and lung capillaries.

items.q: Nephrotic syndrome increases thrombosis risk mainly through urinary loss of what?
o: Antithrombin and altered clotting factor balance
items.exp: Heavy proteinuria loses antithrombin and regulatory proteins while liver overproduces procoagulants, causing venous thrombosis including renal vein thrombosis, classically feared in membranous disease.
r: Incorrect. Platelet counts often rise reactively.
Correct. Antithrombin loss plus procoagulant gain causes clots.
Incorrect. Red cell loss is not the thrombotic mechanism.
Incorrect. Complement loss relates to infection risk more.
items.kp: Nephrotic urine leaks anticoagulants: clots follow, especially membranous.

items.q: Tram track double contour basement membranes with low complement suggest which pattern?
items.exp: Membranoproliferative pattern shows mesangial interposition creating tram track double contours, from immune complex or complement dysregulation (C3 glomerulopathy) needing complement workup.
r: Incorrect. Minimal change shows normal light microscopy.
Correct. Tram tracks mean membranoproliferative pattern.
Incorrect. Thin membranes cause isolated haematuria.
Incorrect. Diabetes thickens membranes with Kimmelstiel Wilson nodules.
items.kp: Tram tracks plus low complement: work up complement pathways.

items.q: Kimmelstiel Wilson nodules with thickened membranes and proteinuria indicate which renal disease?
items.exp: Diabetic nephropathy produces diffuse basement thickening, mesangial expansion and Kimmelstiel Wilson nodules with arteriolar hyalinosis of both afferent and efferent vessels. Congo red negativity separates it from amyloid.
r: Correct. Nodules plus diabetes mean diabetic glomerulosclerosis.
Incorrect. Amyloid stains Congo red with apple green birefringence.
Incorrect. Lupus class II is mesangial immune disease.
Incorrect. Segmental scars define focal segmental sclerosis.
items.kp: Diabetic nodules stain negative for Congo red, unlike amyloid.

items.q: Red cell casts in urine localise bleeding to where?
items.exp: Casts form only inside renal tubules, so red cell casts prove glomerular bleeding with nephritic inflammation. Dysmorphic red cells support the same localisation non invasively.
r: Incorrect. Bladder blood forms clots without tubular casts.
Correct. Casts prove renal glomerular origin.
Incorrect. Urethral bleeding appears at stream start without casts.
Incorrect. Prostatic blood lacks glomerular casts.
items.kp: Casts can only be born in tubules: glomerular bleeding proven.
